Twelve serial files are six surfaces plus seven wrappers
fanout-run has no elapsed upper-bound assertion

label: The twelve serial files are six real test surfaces: seven are 7-line wrappers calling defineAdapterStressSuite, while fanout-run (5925 lines, 171 tests), stress/fanout (843/19), cli-codex (520/26), postflip-fanout (612/4), lineage-timestamp-window (257/5) and db-open-close (97/2) hold the code.
Only four files carry a load-sensitive upper bound on a child process: cli-codex at 1000 ms, stress/fanout at 12000 ms, lineage-timestamp-window at 60000 ms, and db-open-close's 1000 ms lock wait.

db-open-close's second test exists to make two writers contend for one lock, holding it 500 ms in one child and starting a second with zero wait to assert a DB_ERROR exit; cut 5 already gave each file its own lock path, so the requirement is file-local exclusivity.

fanout-run has no assertion bounding elapsed wall time: its timing assertions are string ordering, lower bounds such as completedSlotMs >= 4200, and a 5000 ms waitForFile poll cap, and lower bounds cannot fail under load.
postflip-fanout carries no timing bound at all; it drives the ledger and gateway through execFileSync and asserts state transitions, so its serial placement is not backed by an assertion.
The packet's pre-cut profile measured fanout-run at 157 s, the slowest file in the suite and the largest single block inside the 265 s serial group.

Moving fanout-run and postflip-fanout to the parallel project would drop the serial group from about 265 s to about 108 s against a parallel group already near 240 s, for an estimated suite floor near 348 s instead of 504-511 s, which must be measured.

direction: Removing db-open-close from the serial set
reason: Its second test exists to make two writers contend for one lock; parallel neighbours make the race uncontrolled

direction: Removing lineage-timestamp-window from the serial set
reason: It bounds a child at 60 s and was already raised once for load; the clearest genuine timing dependency

direction: Merging the seven 7-line stress wrappers into one file
reason: No measurable saving and it changes failure reporting granularity

label: The packet records no list of which files failed when every file ran in parallel, so the twelve-file serial set is a blanket precaution rather than a measured set
